title: KMIP Java client interoperability test catalog
purpose: Qualify the same Java client against multiple existing server products and explicit KMIP profiles.
primary_transport: Binary TTLV over mutually authenticated TLS
optional_transports: HTTP JSON TTLV only if shipped as a separately qualified adapter
runtime_rule: Run only the explicitly supported product runtimes; server-inventory.json records which of these apply.

profiles.READ_AES: Get and metadata for independently provisioned AES keys; Query/DiscoverVersions or an explicit fixed profile.
profiles.MANAGE_AES: READ_AES plus supported Create/Register, lifecycle and rotation required by the database.
profiles.TLS_EXPORT: Get supported private-key and X.509 certificate objects, construct Java TLS credentials and complete a handshake.
profiles.WRAPPED_KEYS: Explicitly supported wrapped Get/Register/Import and independently verified unwrap.
profiles.REMOTE_CRYPTO: Explicitly supported Encrypt/Decrypt/Sign/Verify/MAC with independent cryptographic checks.
profiles.TLS_REMOTE: Optional JCA/JSSE provider integration for a remote non-exportable signing key.
profiles.KRYPTON_READ: TLS1.3 AES256 retrieval of administratively provisioned versioned keys.

classification_rules: A required claimed profile with a missing capability fails qualification even if the server returns a well-formed unsupported response.
UNSUPPORTED_SERVER needs recorded versioned evidence; an unexpected failure never auto-updates the manifest.
A normal typed unsupported response may pass the negative-handling case while the corresponding positive feature remains unsupported.

Record the actual execution layer for every result. Controlled-peer and codec results are client-only evidence and never count as live vendor interoperability; split mixed-layer cases into separate execution records.
This file defines the cases. Results are kept in each run's records, never here.

servers.name: PyKMIP
servers.access: Apache 2.0; repeatable local development and CI
servers.setup: Install the pinned package in a Python 3.11 virtual environment; provide a CA, server certificate and client certificate with clientAuth EKU; configure port 5696 and run pykmip-server -f ./server.conf -l ./server.log.
servers.baseline: Binary TTLV with mTLS. Broad key and certificate objects. Existing create/register/get/attribute/lifecycle/sign/encrypt handlers; a version being accepted does not imply every operation is implemented.
servers.limits: No server handlers for ReKey, ReKeyKeyPair, Import, Export, AddAttribute, MACVerify or Check in the inspected tag. Use Register and Get for the basic import/export workflow. No 2.1.
servers.fixture: Two client CN identities; default ownership policy plus one explicit sharing policy. Use INFO logs and an ephemeral database. Disable neither certificate verification nor clientAuth identity checks.
servers.emphasis: Force each of the five wire versions; exercise Register/Get for AES, RSA/EC and X.509; compare same-owner and different-owner access; ensure unsupported operations become typed client errors.

servers.name: OpenKCM Krypton
servers.setup: Deploy required backend and enable its KMIP listener; provision and activate two tenants' AES256 key versions through its administrative API or CLI.
servers.baseline: Reviewed handlers implement raw symmetric Get and GetAttributes; the client certificate CN must match the tenant identity. TLS1.3 is required.
servers.limits: No general KMIP creation/lifecycle or certificate/private-key profile in the reviewed handler. Underlying library versions do not establish application interoperability.
servers.fixture: Known active and inactive UIDs using tenantID:keyID:keyVersion; two client identities; externally rotated and deactivated versions.
servers.emphasis: Read-only profile, opaque IDs with separators, TLS1.2 rejection, wrong tenant, inactive versions, duplicate/unknown attribute requests.

manifest_example.deadline_rule: Overall deadline includes pool waits, retries and backoff and supersedes stage maxima.
manifest_example.limits_rule: Test defaults; validate legitimate certificate/key payload sizes before release.
manifest_example.performance_budget_rule: Required qualification inputs; set from database SLOs before performance gate.

families.title: Fixture readiness and evidence
families.purpose: Establish a trustworthy fixture before attributing any failure to the client.

families.title: TLS and certificate authentication
families.purpose: Validate the transport used to retrieve secrets, independently of KMIP object semantics.

families.title: Binary TTLV and parser boundaries
families.purpose: Use independent vectors and a controlled TLS peer to test the client's decoder and encoder, not a vendor's resilience.

families.title: Version negotiation and schema changes
families.purpose: Each claimed version is a separate tested configuration; negotiation alone proves only one path.

families.title: Discovery attributes and object lookup
families.purpose: Avoid assuming that metadata is ordered, object names are unique or Query is an authorization grant.

families.title: Symmetric keys and export policy
families.purpose: Verify usable cryptographic material and policy outcomes, not merely a successful Get status.

families.title: Private keys certificates and application TLS
families.purpose: Keep application TLS key management distinct from the credentials used to connect to KMIP.

families.title: Lifecycle rotation and authorization
families.purpose: Read back state and material after changes; retrieval policy and lifecycle state are separate assertions.

families.title: Authorization changes and sensitive material
families.purpose: Exercise real effective policy, including restrictions that are distinct from object lifecycle state.

families.title: Optional remote cryptographic operations
families.purpose: Apply this family only to operations intentionally exposed by the Java client; verify cryptographic relationships independently.

families.title: Batch processing and error mapping
families.purpose: Validate partial outcomes and version-specific ordering without assuming every server supports every batch feature.

families.title: Timeouts cancellation and uncertain writes
families.purpose: A transport failure after a write can leave an unknown outcome. Never replay mutations as if correlation IDs guaranteed deduplication.

families.title: Database encryption and recovery
families.purpose: Test complete durable database behavior with the actual client integration, using synthetic data.

families.title: Java API concurrency and resource behavior
families.purpose: Qualify the runtimes and transports actually shipped, not just the default developer JDK.

families.title: Diagnostics secrets and support evidence
families.purpose: Support diagnosis must remain useful without leaking private material.
